title: Center a dual-handle apple wedger over a seated apple and press level through to the board
instruction: Drive the apple wedger level through the seated apple flush onto the cutting board while keeping the apple centered in its cradle, and clear both grippers.
context: Every daily kitchen snack prep or family meal uses handheld fruit slicers and corers to portion apples quickly on a countertop cutting board. Because an 18 N core resistance sits centered 69 mm inward from each side wing handle, pressing only one handle generates an overturning moment that cocks the blade ring past 5 deg and binds it in the fruit, whereas balanced two-sided downward pressure shears cleanly to the board.
setup: A fixed wooden cutting board (170 x 200 x 18 mm, on 2 mm rubber corner feet) sits centered at (0.345, 0.000) m on the station tabletop with a central 77 x 77 x 6 mm walnut-trimmed recessed cradle pocket (well floor 12 mm above tabletop, deck 18 mm above tabletop). A 180 g segmented medium apple specimen (90 g 8-wedge red-skin and cream-flesh body, 72 mm diameter, 58 mm tall, plus a 90 g sliding core anvil with stem and leaf) rests upright inside the cradle pocket; its central core slides vertically across a 48 mm stroke against 18 N yield resistance (4000 N/m stiffness over 4.5 mm deflection before severing). On a fixed dark silicone staging mat (130 x 210 x 3 mm) at (0.200, 0.000) m sits a 210 g dual-wing stainless apple wedger: a 108 mm OD, 98 mm ID 12-sided blade ring (36 mm blade height), an ergonomic upper collar (42 mm total ring height), an 8-sided 23 mm OD (18.4 mm ID) hollow central coring tube, 8 radial 1.8 mm divider blades, and two raised 20 mm-thick cushioned grip spines atop horizontal wing flanges centered at +-69 mm in Y (57 mm above the wedger base, 160 mm handle grip span). One fixed starting layout; arms start at ready pose.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial; the run succeeds once 1.0 holds for 0.5 s. Measured at trial end with a caliper/ruler and digital protractor. 1.0: the apple stays seated within 12 mm of the cradle center and tilted at most 8 deg, the wedger rests within 10 mm radially of the apple, cut depth reached at least 42 mm of the 48 mm stroke against the 18 N (4.5 mm yield) core resistance, the wedger ring sits flush within 4 mm of the cutting board deck tilted at most 5 deg, and both grippers remain more than 120 mm clear of both wedger and apple for 3 s (60 steps). 0.75: full cut flush on deck and clear, hold under 3 s. 0.50: full cut flush on deck, gripper within 120 mm. 0.25: initial cut at least 10 mm, incomplete stroke or not flush/tilted past 5 deg on deck. 0 otherwise (doing nothing, sweeping, dropping off-center, or 1-hand cocked jam). Possible scores: 0.0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Lift the wedger off the cutting board, reset the apple core anvil back to full 58 mm crown height inside the 77 mm recessed board cradle, and place the wedger level on the dark staging mat at x = 0.200 m, y = 0.000 m with its handles aligned along Y.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (PhysX, 20 Hz control). The apple is modelled as an 8-wedge rigid body around a vertical prismatic core slide with an irreversible 18 N (4000 N/m, 4.5 mm yield) severing law instead of continuous deformable fruit tissue; the wedger uses 12-sided/8-sided primitive rings, 8 radial blades, and flanged wing handles. Friction and contact softness are calibrated within 0.8x to 1.5x margin.
